(a) the most appropriate method of anesthesia in CCP is general anesthesia; (b) the most appropriate anesthetic agent is sevoflurane; (c) the most appropriate muscle relaxant in CCP is atracurium; and (d) the most appropriate analgesic in CCP is fentanyl.
the choice of anesthetic technique in CCP depends on the type of surgery, its duration, and the presence or absence of concomitant pathology.

the use of general anesthesia is not recommended in patients with CCP, and the use of local anesthetics is not recommended in children under 3 years old, as well as in patients with CCP with a high risk of developing complications.
